gaps.sentence: He suggested ___ a taxi instead of walking.
gaps.explanation: suggest + -ing (no infinitive with a person: suggest that we take is also possible).
deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: He's considering ___ his job and travelling for a year.
You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: Try ___ the handle — sometimes it sticks.
gaps.explanation: try + -ing = experiment with a method; try to do = make an effort.

gaps.sentence: He's not used to ___ so early.
gaps.explanation: be used TO + -ing: not used to getting (it's a habit he isn't accustomed to).
